blocks.evidence: Repeated runtime dispatch target; 59-step single-instruction trace executes this block to JMP 0x58D870E8.
blocks.uncertainty: Basic-block extent on the observed path, not a function boundary. VM opcode semantics and whole-VM equivalence are unknown; trap-flag instrumentation may affect code that observes TF indirectly.

blocks.evidence: Second runtime JMP ESI target in a three-dispatch trace. Single-stepped instructions at 0x58BEB131 and 0x58BEB135 decode as MOV EDX,[EBP] and JMP 0x58BCA099; the next observed IP is 0x58BCA099.
blocks.uncertainty: Nine-byte executed basic block only; the trampoline at 0x58BCA099 is outside this block. The bytecode operation meaning and subsequent VM state are unresolved. The instruction trace sets EFLAGS.TF.

blocks.evidence: Third runtime JMP ESI target in two repeated four-dispatch traces. The executed path reads a dword through [EBP], adds four to EBP, then directly jumps to 0x58D5FED9.
blocks.uncertainty: Fifteen-byte executed basic block only; subsequent trampoline path is outside this block. Opcode semantics and VM state after the path are unresolved. The instruction trace sets EFLAGS.TF.

blocks.evidence: Fourth runtime JMP ESI target in two repeated five-dispatch traces. The 46 traced instructions run sequentially from 0x58C85B6B through the terminal direct JMP at 0x58C85BF9, which transfers to 0x58C9884B.
blocks.uncertainty: 147-byte executed basic block only; trampoline code beginning at 0x58C9884B is outside it. Opaque arithmetic/flag operations prevent assigning VM opcode semantics. The instruction trace sets EFLAGS.TF.

blocks.evidence: Fifth runtime JMP ESI target in two repeated six-dispatch traces. The executed instruction sequence starts at 0x58C0E4F5 and ends in a direct JMP at 0x58C0E535 to 0x58D8AF3E.
blocks.uncertainty: Sixty-nine-byte executed basic block only. Subsequent VM trampoline flow is outside the block; opaque register and flag operations do not establish opcode semantics. The instruction trace sets EFLAGS.TF, and this block executes PUSHFD then POP [EDI], so TF is written into VM data and the observed data side effect is not representative of an uninstrumented run.
